document_check.note: Lei B, Zhu Y, Yu S, et al. Multi-scale enhanced graph convolutional network for mild cognitive impairment detection. Pattern Recognition 2023;134:109106 (available online October 2022). The paper is an MSE-GCN that fuses rs-fMRI functional and DTI structural connectivity, applied to 184 ADNI subjects. This matches 'multi-scale graph convolution over functional and structural connectivity (Lei et al. 2022)'.

cited_result: The context cites the method rather than a number. The principal result appraised is the leave-one-out cross-validated classification performance of the MSE-GCN on fused DTI and rs-fMRI connectivity: accuracy 85.42% for EMCI vs NC, 93.46% for LMCI vs NC, 92.31% for LMCI vs EMCI and 83.11% for the three-class task (abstract: mean accuracy 90.39%).
tool_reason: The result is the diagnostic performance of a machine-learning classifier, which is prediction-model performance.

domains.rationale: Participants were sampled by diagnostic group from ADNI (40 LMCI, 77 EMCI, 67 NC), which is a case-control type selection. No inclusion or exclusion criteria are reported, and neither is the way these 184 were chosen from the database.

signalling.question: 1.1 Were appropriate data sources used?
signalling.quote: 40 late mild cognitive impairment (LMCI) patients, 77 early mild cognitive impairment (EMCI) patients, and 67 normal controls (NC) are obtained from the ADNI dataset

signalling.question: 1.2 Were all inclusions and exclusions of participants appropriate?
signalling.quote: Searched Section 3.1 and Table 2 for selection criteria, the scan-availability requirement and the sampling method. Only group counts, sex and age are given (Table 2 summarizes the subjects’ information in this study.)

domains.rationale: Connectivity features come from standard automated pipelines applied identically to all subjects, and imaging, age and sex would be available at the time of use.

signalling.question: 2.1 Were predictors defined and assessed in a similar way for all participants?
signalling.quote: The R-fMRI data preprocessing procedure is performed using GRETNA [47]. (page 4); The DTI data preprocessing procedure is performed using PANDA with five steps [50]. (page 5)

signalling.question: 2.2 Were predictor assessments made without knowledge of outcome data?
signalling.quote: Features were derived by automated pipelines: Finally, we obtain the time series of each individual ROI of each subject via the time series over all voxels in particular ROI.

signalling.question: 2.3 Are all predictors available at the time the model is intended to be used?
signalling.quote: both image data (e.g., R-fMRI and DTI) and non-image data (e.g., gender and age) are utilized to construct a sparse graph

domains.rationale: The EMCI, LMCI and NC labels are taken from ADNI with no description of the diagnostic criteria, who applied them, or the timing relative to the scans.

signalling.question: 3.1 Was the outcome determined appropriately?
signalling.quote: Searched Sections 3 and 4 for how the diagnostic labels were assigned; the only statement is that subjects 'are obtained from the ADNI dataset'.

signalling.question: 3.2 Was a pre-specified or standard outcome definition used?
signalling.quote: No diagnostic criteria for EMCI, LMCI or NC are stated anywhere in the text.

signalling.question: 3.3 Were predictors excluded from the outcome definition?
signalling.quote: Without the diagnostic criteria it cannot be established whether imaging contributed to the labels.

signalling.question: 3.4 Was the outcome defined and determined in a similar way for all participants?
signalling.quote: Searched for the labelling procedure; not reported.

signalling.question: 3.5 Was the outcome determined without knowledge of predictor information?
signalling.quote: Searched for blinding of diagnosis to imaging; not reported.

signalling.question: 3.6 Was the time interval between predictor assessment and outcome determination appropriate?
signalling.quote: Searched for the interval between the DTI/rs-fMRI scans and the diagnostic visit; not reported.

domains.rationale: The sample is very small for a deep graph network (184 subjects, 40 LMCI, 500 features). The random-walk step p and the Chebyshev order K were chosen from the same leave-one-out results that are then reported, and grid search is not described as nested. The transductive population graph contains the held-out subject. No calibration is reported, class imbalance is not addressed, and there is no external validation. The F1 values for the same configuration differ between Table 3 and Table 4.

signalling.question: 4.1 Were there a reasonable number of participants with the outcome?
signalling.quote: For all GCN-based competing methods, we use the same model parameters: 20% dropout rate, 10 −5 wt of the l 2 regularization term, 0.002 learning rate, and 500 features. (page 5); Since ADNI is a relatively small dataset (page 5)

signalling.question: 4.2 Were continuous and categorical predictors handled appropriately?
signalling.quote: Features are continuous LWCC values; age enters edge weights through a threshold: where β is the standard deviation of the subjects’ ages.

signalling.question: 4.3 Were all enrolled participants included in the analysis?
signalling.quote: We use a total number of 184 subjects in this study.

signalling.question: 4.4 Were participants with missing data handled appropriately?
signalling.quote: Searched for missing scans, failed preprocessing or missing demographics; nothing reported.

signalling.question: 4.5 Was selection of predictors based on univariable analysis avoided?
signalling.quote: How the '500 features' were chosen, and whether inside the cross-validation folds, is not described.

signalling.question: 4.6 Were complexities in the data accounted for appropriately?
signalling.quote: we can obtain λ + 1 feature vectors F composed of LWCC when λ FCs and one SC are obtained from a subject

signalling.question: 4.7 Were relevant model performance measures evaluated appropriately (including calibration)?
signalling.quote: The performance is evaluated and compared by mean values of classification accuracy ( ACC ), sensitivity ( SEN ), specificity ( SPEC ), and F-score (F1).

signalling.question: 4.8 Were overfitting, underfitting and optimism in model performance accounted for?
signalling.quote: model at different scales and select the best scale p from the average cross-validation results. ... Therefore, we set the optimal p as 5. (page 8); Also, grid search is applied to select optimal parameters for all methods. (page 5)

signalling.question: 4.9 Do predictors and their assigned weights in the final model correspond to the results from the reported multivariable analysis?
signalling.quote: Network weights are not reported. Table 3 gives F1 84.67 for Ours(F) EMCI vs NC, while Table 4 gives F1 89.98 for LWCC in the same task and configuration.

signalling.question: AI: Is the train/test split at the participant level?
signalling.quote: we use a leave one-out (LOO) cross-validation strategy for all experiments to conduct fair comparisons (one feature vector per subject)

signalling.question: AI: Are preprocessing, feature selection and hyperparameter tuning done within the training folds only?
signalling.quote: all subjects are represented by using a sparse graph (denoted as an MCI-graph), in which each vertex denotes a subject’s features (page 2). Hyperparameters p and K were chosen from cross-validated results (page 8).

signalling.question: AI: Is the test set held out from all tuning?
signalling.quote: when K = 4, the model obtains the best classification results (the same LOOCV folds supply both the tuning and the reported performance)

signalling.question: AI: Is class imbalance handled?
signalling.quote: Groups of 40 LMCI, 77 EMCI and 67 NC; searched for weighting or resampling and found none.

signalling.question: AI: Is reported performance apparent, internally or externally validated?
signalling.quote: Four groups of detection experiments and comparison with the state-of-the-art methods have been conducted on ADNI dataset

overall_rationale: Domain 1 (case-control sampling) and domain 4 (very small sample, hyperparameters tuned on the reported cross-validation, no calibration, no external validation) are high risk, and domain 3 is unclear.

applicability.rationale: Diagnostic groups were selected from a research database, not a clinical or screening population.
Needs both DTI and rs-fMRI research acquisitions.
The label definitions are not reported.
